newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ -- Florida crop seen meeting domestic demand.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ -- Florida crop seen meeting domestic demand.

text.p: The Florida orange crop should be large enough to meet demand for frozen concentrated orange juice and continue to put pressure on imports, the Florida Department of Citrus said.

"We anticipate that as the Florida crop continues to grow, there will be less reliance on imports," Dan Santangelo, executive director of the Florida Department of Agriculture, said in a conference call with reporters following the release of the USDA's crop estimate.

Santangelo put imports at 25 million boxes for the 1996/97 season. The USDA pegged the Florida crop at 220.0 million 90-lb boxes compared with 203.2 million boxes last year, an eight percent increase.
Yields rose to 1.53 gallons per box from 1.52 gallons last season, the USDA said.
The estimate was seen as neutral to slightly bearish for prices.
